Everything you need to ship from India to Panama or import from Panama to India: the trade agreement, routes and transit times, how your buyer imports, duties, regulators and documents.
India and Panama at a glance
A regional hub: the Colón Free Zone re-exports Indian goods (textiles, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, motorcycles, auto parts) across the Americas. India buys small volumes.
Routes and transit times to Panama
30–40 days to Colón or Manzanillo. A key transhipment hub for the Caribbean and the west coast.
Transit times are indicative port-to-port from Nhava Sheva / Mundra (sea) and Delhi / Mumbai (air). Routing changes (for example Red Sea diversions) can add 10–14 days.
Importing into Panama: what your buyer needs
A licensed customs broker (corredor de aduanas) files the declaration with the ANA.
The Colón Free Zone allows duty-free storage and re-export to the whole region.

From Panama to India, and tips from the field
File the Bill of Entry through a licensed customs broker in India (YAM holds licence R-7/92).
Check the HS code in the Indian tariff, the DGFT import policy (free, restricted or prohibited) and any BIS, FSSAI, plant quarantine or other permit before the goods ship.
If an agreement applies, get the correct certificate of origin from the exporter to claim the lower duty.
Selling to the Colón Free Zone is often the easiest way into smaller Caribbean and Central American markets.
